'''Sir Eric James Denton''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|size=100%|CBE|FRS}} (30 September 1923 – 2 January 2007)<ref name="Indie">{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/professor-sir-eric-denton-433857.html|title=Professor Sir Eric Denton|last=Brownlee|first=Colin|work=Obituary|publisher=The Independent Newspaper|access-date=2008-12-06 | location=London | date=27 January 2007}}</ref> was a British marine biologist who won the Royal Society's [[Royal Medal]] in 1987.<ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Clarke | first1 = M. R. | doi = 10.1098/rsbm.2009.0001 | title = Sir Eric James Denton CBE. 30 September 1923 -- 2 January 2007 | journal = [[Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society]] | volume = 55 | pages = 59–76 | year = 2009 | doi-access = free }}</ref>

Denton was born in [[Bentley, South Yorkshire]].<ref name="Indie"/> He was educated at [[Doncaster Grammar School]] and [[St John's College, Cambridge]], where he graduated with an Ordinary degree in Physics, before pursuing biophysics research at [[University College London]].<ref name="WhosWho">{{Who's Who | title=DENTON, Sir Eric (James) | id = U13514 | type = was | volume = 2020 | edition = online}}</ref> He was subsequently a lecturer in Physiology at the [[University of Aberdeen]], and then a physiologist at the [[Marine Biological Association]] Laboratory in Plymouth. From 1974 to 1987 he was the Director of the Marine Biological Association Laboratory.<ref name="WhosWho"/>

Denton died in St Just, Cornwall on 2 January 2007.<ref name="Indie"/>
